name: Loot drops with rarity beams
oneLiner: Defeated foes and opened chests pop loot that arcs out with a ground shadow, lands with a bounce on free ground (landing spot and whole flight path tested against the game's walls, never off the map), then shows a light beam and glowing outline in its rarity colour and a small name tag; items in reach fly to the player on a clear line and are picked up exactly once with a flash. Rarities, items and drop tables are plain data; name tags never overlap each other, the HUD or open windows and glide or crossfade instead of jumping. Crisp pixel icons and a bitmap font on pixel canvases, shaded icons and soft beams on HD canvases (or a painted icon atlas).
fits: top-down action RPGs and dungeon crawlers
twin-stick and arena games with drops
top-down adventure games with chests and foes
horde survival games (gold and gems that magnet to the hero)
notFor: side-view platformers (the throw uses a fake height over a ground plane; side view is not covered by the checks)
menu-only battles with no map to drop on (drop on the map after the fight instead)
games where loot must stay a secret until chosen (reward screens: use an upgrade or shop element)

needs: the game's wall / water test in world px (and its tile size), the map bounds
where foes die and chests open (a drop call, once each), and what the game already drops
the player's feet in world px, the camera, the view rect and every HUD box / open window (uiRects)
a fixed update step (also run by the ?t= replay), update(0) while the world is stopped
a ground pass between floor and sprites, a pass after sprites, a tag pass before the HUD
provides: onPickup(drop) once per item (the game decides what it gives), onLand
rects() of the name tags for other overlays
list(), audit() (items in walls, must be 0), stats(), hash() for checks

assets: module/loot-beams.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_LootBeams): drop tables and rarity rolls, wall-safe throw planning, flight with bounce, magnet and pickup, beam / outline / flash drawing, built-in icons shaded per pixel (10 keys), a 5-row bitmap font, the name-tag layout
optional: a painted icon atlas of the game's own (the demo reuses elements/painted-ui/assets/kit/icons.webp)
